[2632] To strengthen protection against external cyber attacks, efforts can be beneficially directed towards rapid identification of new or existing types of attacks and active countermeasures that can help prevent Danish networks from being compromised

[2633] The current national strategy for cyber and information security is being implemented and has, among other things, resulted in new legislation in the cyber area

[2634] A new national strategy is expected to be prepared for 2017-18, and there will continue to be a need for increased focus and strengthening of the area, possibly with new regulation, as digital threats develop

[2635] It is crucial for the protection of Denmark and Danish interests that the Danish Defense Intelligence Service, including the Center for Cybersecurity, has the necessary tools and technological capacity to detect, prevent and counter threats at all times

[2636] RECOMMENDATIONS – CYBER CAPACITY

[2637] Increase focus on cyber skills and training at all levels, including possible consideration of a cyber training capacity at the Danish Defence Academy

[2638] Strengthen Danish authorities' ability to communicate securely, for example through a national Danish solution for securing highly classified communications

[2639] Initiate an investigation to identify opportunities to further limit Danish society's vulnerability to cyber activities

[2640] The Home Guard Today, the Home Guard consists of approximately 50,000 volunteer members, of which approximately 15,000 are active

[2641] The members can perform a wide range of important tasks from surveillance and guarding to actual military operations. Personnel and units from the Home Guard have increasingly participated in the defense's national task solving on land, at sea and in the air, such as ammunition clearance, surveillance, search and guarding

[2642] The Home Guard has for periods relieved the army of its tasks in international missions, including in Kosovo and Afghanistan, where personnel were deployed as integrated parts of army units

[2643] In the event of a military crisis where Denmark is to be used as a base and staging area for NATO, the Home Guard will be able to contribute to creating the necessary depth in the defense and solve a number of manpower-intensive tasks

[2644] The Home Guard already participates to a certain extent in stabilization efforts in fragile states with a view to capacity building, military support for civilian reconstruction and support for humanitarian efforts

[2645] Here, it is a particular advantage for the Home Guard that the members can also use their various civilian skills

[2646] Among other things, the Home Guard has a database of the competencies available among the volunteers

[2647] The efforts are coordinated with the other actors under the Ministries of Defence and Foreign Affairs, but the integrated thinking should be increased. ter

[2648] In relation to capacity building, efforts should be focused in particular where Danish interests are at stake, for example building the capacities of local authorities in Denmark and Europe's eastern and southern neighbouring areas

[2649] Furthermore, refugee and migration flows and the changed security situation in Europe and the Baltic Sea region may mean a need to reconsider crisis preparedness and the area of civil protection, which has also received renewed focus in NATO

[2650] This development will lead to a future increased demand for specially trained rescue personnel and expertise as well as special equipment, including for operations in Arctic climates

[2651] The role of the Armed Forces in the Arctic

[2652] In light of the increasing activity in the Arctic and an increased need for the defense to perform tasks in the region, a general increase in the priority of the effort is recommended

[2653] A central task for the Home Guard is to assist the police and other civil authorities, including with guarding and searching

[2654] The need for support for the police in connection with anti-terrorist operations or when handling migrants and refugees, etc. means that the use of units from the Home Guard and the Armed Forces can be advantageously further integrated to align operational requirements and consideration for the civilian population

[2655] It is clear from the current defense agreement that the Home Guard must strengthen its ability to support and assist the defense, and work has been initiated to involve the defense reserve personnel and the Home Guard volunteers to a greater extent in the operational task solving

[2656] Operational cooperation currently takes place between two independent agencies

[2657] This entails considerable formal and administrative coordination and is an obstacle to effective task solving

[2658] A unified management and coordination of the authorities that directly handle the core military tasks would mean administrative simplification as well as operational gains and greater flexibility in the overall defense

[2659] RECOMMENDATIONS – ARCTIC

[2660] That a special financial framework to strengthen the defence's task performance in the Arctic of at least DKK 120 million annually be continued in the upcoming defence agreement

[2661] RECOMMENDATIONS – HOME GUARD

[2662] Integrate the Home Guard Command into the Joint Defence Command at the same level as the Army Staff, the Navy Staff, the Air Staff, etc

[2663] It will be crucial to preserve the character of the Home Guard as a voluntary and popularly rooted organization

[2664] In addition, a civilian committee can be maintained in the Home Guard structure as well as a special law on the Home Guard

[2665] Maintain a separate main account for the Home Guard in the Finance Act

[2666] Integrate and coordinate the Home Guard's stabilization efforts

[2667] further with other Danish stabilization efforts, cf. section

[2668] To strengthen the defense's surveillance capabilities to create an improved situational picture for use in, among other things, sovereignty enforcement, rescue and handling of environmental tasks

[2669] In this context, it is recommended to investigate the possibilities of establishing a satellite data download station in Greenland in order to continuously obtain a more updated situational picture and better opportunities to exchange data with partner countries

[2670] To strengthen the defense's communication platforms in the Arctic region

[2671] The possibilities should therefore be explored for a public/private partnership on a satellite-based solution in the Arctic to supply both the defense and civil society with broadband connections and improved communication solutions in general

[2672] A first step will be to prepare a business case that identifies future civil and commercial needs as well as the defense's future needs for communication solutions

[2673] To strengthen the Arctic Command by establishing a voluntary unit in Greenland, based on the Home Guard Act and in cooperation with the Greenlandic authorities, which will be organizationally anchored in the Arctic Command

[2674] In parallel, it is recommended to establish a voluntary reporting service and marine environment watchdog scheme, where the Arctic Command establishes capacity to receive reports in connection with searches, environmental tasks and other observations from the civilian population

[2675] The Danish Emergency Management Agency's international tasks primarily include efforts in connection with specific disasters and building capacity among authorities in fragile areas so that they are better able to handle disaster situations themselves

[2676] The Danish Emergency Management Agency has also contributed to, among other things, the transport of chemical substances from Syria and the Ebola response in Sierra Leone

[2677] The Danish Emergency Management Agency must continue to be ready to contribute to sudden disasters worldwide, for example, severe natural disasters

[2678] In an increasingly densely populated world with climate change and increasing pressure on energy and water supplies, disasters are expected to become more widespread

[2679] And the ash cloud in 2010 or the simultaneous earthquake, tsunami and nuclear incident in Japan in 2011 have shown how unforeseen situations can arise

[2680] International disaster and emergency response activities must be continuously integrated with other Danish international activities

[2681] The way forward for Denmark's interests and values Chapter 7 brings together the threads of five future core tasks and their realization through increased integration of foreign policy instruments

[2682] The chapter presents a proposal for mechanisms that can ensure strategic coordination across authorities and policy areas and a political and popular anchoring that can strengthen continuity in foreign policy

[2683] Denmark's strategic orientation The way forward for safeguarding Denmark's national interests and values ​​is an interest-based foreign policy that - based on Denmark's strategic orientation - focuses and gathers forces where the stakes are highest and where Denmark can make a real difference - alone or in partnership with others

[2684] The starting point for Denmark's strategic orientation is our European identity, EU membership and the Nordic community of values, the location of Greenland and the Faroe Islands in North America and the North Atlantic, as well as our strong bilateral relationship with the United States

[2685] In addition, we have strategic partnerships with China and other Asian countries

[2686] This provides a unique opportunity to position Denmark strategically with three pillars: ▪

[2687] A European dimension

[2688] With the EU as our focal point, we must maintain relations with our closest European ally, Germany – but also continue to have strong ties with the UK and France

[2689] We can strengthen the European dimension by building a strategic cooperation based on the common interest we have with the Nordic and Baltic countries as well as the Netherlands, which can pull European cooperation in a Northern European direction

[2690] A transatlantic dimension

[2691] We must be a transatlantic voice in NATO and the EU and leverage our close relations with the United States to build bridges and strengthen transatlantic ties

[2692] We must utilize our position as an Arctic power to influence developments in the Arctic for the benefit of the Kingdom, the region and the Greenlandic and Faroese people

[2693] An Asian dimension

[2694] We must build an Asian dimension and leverage our strategic partnerships to advance our commercial interests and global agendas

[2695] This dimension should be strengthened by building a strategic partnership with India

[2696] Together, these three dimensions are a strong starting point for safeguarding the strategic interests identified in Chapter 4 towards 2030. Core tasks and priorities We are in a time of transition characterized by political and economic shifts in power, a changing threat landscape and a more connected world, which is increasingly characterized by new actors with global ambitions

[2697] There is thus a lot to tackle, but the implementation of significant savings in the public sector, including in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, creates a need to prioritize and focus efforts to ensure optimal protection of Denmark's interests

[2698] This must be done in such a way that the foreign service does not become “discount diplomacy”, but on the contrary, “diplomacy that counts”

[2699] This year, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has carried out a reprioritization, in which areas of responsibility have been downgraded or removed from priority, offices have been merged, and embassies have been closed

[2700] However, there is also a need to strategically identify the core tasks and priorities that should be prioritized to promote Denmark's interests, including commercial ones

[2701] On this basis, five benchmarks can be identified for Denmark's external policy areas: The immediate area: Actively promote sustainable and peaceful development in the Kingdom's immediate areas in the Arctic and the Baltic Sea region by prioritizing efforts and strengthening and developing cooperation structures and the capacity to be at the forefront of opportunities and threats

[2702] ▪ Europe: Take responsibility for peace, stability and prosperity in Europe and Europe's surrounding areas by, in particular, actively contributing to an EU that is able to collectively handle crises and exercise global influence, contribute to the fight against terrorism and secure Denmark's position as a core member of credible NATO cooperation and as a transatlantic bridge builder

[2703] Refugees and migration

[2704] Prevent uncontrolled flows by strengthening the integration of foreign policy, regional interventions, stabilization efforts, humanitarian assistance and long-term development cooperation to promote security, economic development and good governance, especially in fragile states in the Middle East, North Africa and Afghanistan

[2705] ▪ Economic diplomacy: Contribute to Danish growth, prosperity and innovation by conducting active economic diplomacy that positions Denmark strongly in the rapid business development, supports the internationalization, competitiveness and exports of the business community and society's ability to attract investments, knowledge and talents from all over the world

[2706] ▪ Global goods: Promote global solutions and handling of future climate challenges by, based on Danish positions of strength, values and interests, taking the lead in implementing the UN 2030 Agenda and the Paris Climate Agreement and supporting rules-based international cooperation, where both old and new powers will continue to see the UN as the primary global framework for balancing interests

[2707] These five benchmarks constitute a comprehensive strategic proposal for core tasks and priorities to promote Denmark's interests. Integrated thinking and coordination of Denmark's foreign policy All five benchmarks are characterised by the fact that there are increasingly close links between the internal development of Danish society and external developments

[2708] They largely cross traditional boundaries between foreign, security, defense, trade, and development policy

[2709] Thus, the solutions must also cut across existing boundaries within and between ministries and authorities, and they should increasingly involve actors from across society. 7.3.1 An integrated foreign policy Both the formulation and implementation of Denmark's diplomatic and defense policy areas of focus should be seen as a whole

[2710] Therefore, Denmark should, to a much greater extent than today, have a coherent foreign policy

[2711] A more strategic approach to foreign policy is a prerequisite if everyone from the political and strategic level to the executive levels is to pull in the same direction across organizational dividing lines

[2712] This can be achieved with a more forward-looking strategic planning of foreign policy priorities, a broader and earlier involvement of stakeholders in the decision-making basis in individual cases, and by improving the decision-making procedures for the planning of Denmark's policy that apply in the government and in relation to the Folketing

[2713] This can create a common thread for the overall Danish foreign policy effort, from discussions in the Folketing to the government's decisions to the executive levels across ministries and authorities

[2714] To achieve this, a number of measures should be implemented, which are described below

[2715] The measures are internally linked and will thus be able to mutually support each other

[2716] A national foreign and security policy strategy Denmark's foreign policy impact can be strengthened by establishing a prioritized and strategic organization of the overall foreign and security policy area of action in a forward-looking prioritization document

[2717] The document can take the form of a broad national foreign and security policy strategy that encompasses the entire range of external instruments – foreign, security, defense, trade, and development policy

[2718] The determination and balancing of the various elements of such a strategy is ultimately a political decision to be made by the government

[2719] But the basis for the political decision, the preparation of analyses, etc., should be provided in close collaboration with all key stakeholders

[2720] The document and process can contribute to a more sustainable focus of tasks and resources and an ongoing public discussion of how we best care for Denmark's interests

[2721] More long-term thinking will make it possible to better unleash Denmark's potential with a view to fully exploiting new opportunities and handling diplomatic and defense policy challenges and risks

[2722] This can bring Denmark to the forefront of international developments and create a basis for initiatives that create solutions to new challenges

[2723] The strategy document should include the following elements: Establishing the vision for Denmark's foreign, security and defence policy

[2724] The national interests to be safeguarded ▪

[2725] An analysis of international developments (threats, challenges, opportunities) ▪

[2726] Strategic prioritization of the use of foreign, security and development policy, trade policy and defense policy instruments, including the defense's operations budget. Area strategies should be formulated across ministries

[2727] The strategies must cover the Danish efforts to implement the five benchmarks identified in section

[2728] In these strategies, the various instruments and policy areas are integrated and all relevant ministries and authorities are involved in the process with a view to ensuring full ownership and follow-up across the government

[2729] These should be short and concise strategies (approximately five pages), approved at government level and serving as a strategic framework for the specific, implemented policy across authorities, and updated as needed

[2730] In addition, strategies can be prepared as needed regarding specific geographical or thematic areas where special Danish interests have been identified, and there must be a focus on specific Danish priority objectives, instruments and means

[2731] An example is the preparation of a biannual forward-looking strategy for Denmark's priorities in the area of ​​European policy

[2732] The internal decision-making process – coordinated government decisions The government has asked for a comprehensive proposal for stronger coordination and integrated thinking of Denmark's foreign and security policy, defense policy, trade policy and export promotion, and development policy

[2733] This can be achieved by improving the decision-making procedures in the government and in relation to the Folketing, which form the framework for determining Denmark's policy

[2734] There is currently no dedicated government committee or other forum – with the participation of relevant ministers and stakeholders – as a framework for the government's political and strategic discussions on the organization of our diplomatic and defense policy efforts

[2735] Today, the government's foreign, security and defense policy decisions are primarily made in the government's Coordination Committee after consideration in the preparatory Coordination Committee

[2736] The permanent members of the Coordination Committee are the Prime Minister, the Minister of Foreign Affairs and the Minister of Finance, and it is expanded ad hoc with other relevant ministers

[2737] Discussions about, for example, the deployment of forces to international missions are generally prepared in collaboration between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Defence, which prepare written proposals for decision

[2738] The current decision-making process does not systematically ensure that decisions are considered in a sufficient strategic context and that there is the necessary time for strategic discussions

[2739] Decisions thus risk appearing ad hoc

[2740] For example, there is no forward-looking political prioritization of the defense's operations budget

[2741] And the decision-making basis for contributions to international military operations is prepared – and the decisions are made – without necessarily directly involving all key stakeholders

[2742] The formal responsibility for monitoring and ensuring the implementation of the government's foreign, security and defence policy decisions lies with the relevant minister

[2743] Establishment of a foreign policy forum

[2744] To ensure better coordination and integrated thinking, it is proposed to establish a foreign policy government forum with responsibility for the government's political and strategic planning of Denmark's international efforts with the following focus: ▪ Determining the national foreign and security policy strategy ▪ Determining the regional strategies, etc

[2745] Diplomatic and defense policy initiatives ▪ Consolidated decisions with greater foreign policy reach ▪

[2746] The European political strategy ▪

[2747] Strategic organization of economic diplomacy

[2748] The foreign policy forum should be composed of the central, relevant ministers, including the Prime Minister (as needed), the Minister of Foreign Affairs (also in the capacity of Minister for Development and Trade), the Minister of Defence, the Minister of Justice, the Minister of Business and Growth, the Minister of Immigration, Integration and Housing, and the Minister of Finance, and could be expanded with relevant ministers, for example when economic diplomacy or European policy issues are on the agenda

[2749] This ensures coordinated decisions across foreign, security, defense, development and trade policy

[2750] This can contribute to foreign and security policy decisions being raised to a greater political level and made on a strategic basis with well-founded options

[2751] It can also contribute to prioritizing topics, so that there is room for both concrete decisions and time-consuming strategic discussions on selected issues

[2752] At the same time, an opportunity is created for a political discussion of the overall strategic European policy priorities

[2753] Furthermore, economic diplomacy, which cuts across several ministerial areas, is anchored at the government level

[2754] Finally, the involvement of all key stakeholders in the decision-making process and in relation to the distribution of responsibilities and follow-up is ensured. Such a forum can either take the form of a government committee, the government's Foreign and Security Policy Committee, or a National Foreign and Security Council, or a combination of the models

[2755] The model of establishing a government committee on foreign and security policy issues will function in the same way as other government committees with the Minister for Foreign Affairs as chairman and with the participation of the above-mentioned ministers

[2756] When the Prime Minister participates in the committee meetings – typically when the committee deals with matters of the same nature as the foreign policy matters currently dealt with in the Coordination Committee – the Prime Minister should, however, be the chairman. To prepare the government's discussions, a preparatory committee at department head level may be established, chaired by the Prime Minister or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (depending on the agenda), where all relevant ministries and authorities, including, for example, the Joint Defence Command and the intelligence services, are represented

[2757] The basis for the preparatory discussions can be established in various fora

[2758] The strategic European policy discussions can thus be prepared in the government's EU Committee, while the strategic discussions on the organization of economic diplomacy, for example, can be prepared in the interministerial Coordination Group on Economic Diplomacy with the involvement of business and other stakeholders through the Foreign Economic Forum

[2759] The development policy discussions can be organized with the involvement of the Development Policy Council

[2760] For the purpose of coordinating the committee's affairs, a secretariat function should be attached to the committee

[2761] This secretariat can be located in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs with representatives from other relevant ministries and authorities attached

[2762] With the right composition and managerial focus, such a secretariat will be able to seek to drive integrated thinking, both at the strategic and executive level

[2763] An alternative to a traditional government committee is the establishment of a National Foreign and Security Council with the same composition as the government committee, but with key officials participating in the meetings, including the heads of the intelligence services and the Chief of Defence

[2764] To support the National Foreign and Security Council, a function as a national foreign and security advisor with a small secretariat attached is being established or developed

[2765] The advisor will be tasked with leading the preparation of drafts for the government's national security strategy and other strategy documents, developing foreign policy initiatives and driving the preparation of the government's discussions and decisions in the council and ensuring their implementation

[2766] To support the preparatory work, the advisor may involve the relevant ministries and other authorities that are stakeholders in a given case

[2767] If necessary, the function should be anchored in the Prime Minister's Office to obtain the necessary overview and the necessary weight to bring all relevant actors into play across the various organizations

[2768] It can either be assigned to an existing function in the Prime Minister's Office or established as an independent function

[2769] The external decision-making process – Parliament's involvement

[2770] It is the government that conducts the Kingdom's foreign policy

[2771] This must be done in accordance with the procedures for the involvement of the Folketing that follow from the Constitution

[2772] With respect to this, it is proposed that the government present its foreign and security policy strategy in the Folketing with a view to a political discussion and to achieving broad political support and ownership of the established priorities for Danish foreign policy

[2773] The involvement of the Folketing in the planning of Denmark's international engagement can be achieved by the government presenting its national foreign and security policy strategy to the Folketing as a basis for a forward-looking parliamentary debate on the Kingdom's foreign, security and defence policy priorities in the coming period

[2774] This will give political parties the opportunity to relate to the organization of policy

[2775] At the same time, it will be a procedure that ensures a public discussion of Denmark's foreign policy situation, the Kingdom's interests and future priorities

[2776] Such an approach will strengthen continuity in Denmark's foreign policy

[2777] The debate may be concluded with a parliamentary resolution on the majority's position on the presented strategy

[2778] Such a broad parliamentary debate on the prioritization of the entire foreign, security and defense policy area could also replace the current, more retrospective foreign policy statements, which do not provide sufficient opportunity for forward-looking, strategic discussions of Denmark's interests and foreign policy

[2779] Furthermore, the Folketing may consider coordinating its international activities, including committee trips, more actively with the elements of the national foreign and security policy strategy and with the timing of any Danish efforts

[2780] This will ensure that the Folketing's focus and knowledge can be put to best use in relation to Denmark's interests

[2781] Conclusion In the terms of reference, the government expressed the wish that the investigation work should lead to three things: An identification of Denmark's strategic interests in light of a number of key development trends, challenges and opportunities in the coming 10-15 years, An overall strategic proposal for core tasks and priorities to promote Denmark's interests in the coming years

[2782] A comprehensive proposal for stronger coordination and integrated thinking of Denmark's foreign and security policy, defense policy, trade policy and export promotion, and development policy

[2783] According to the terms of reference, the report will, among other things, form the basis for upcoming negotiations on a new defense agreement after 2017 and for a new development policy strategy in

[2784] Against this background, Chapter 1 presents a model in which Denmark's interests can serve as directional arrows for prioritizing foreign policy, just as the international development trends in which Denmark must navigate in the coming 10-15 years are presented in Chapter

[2785] Chapter 3 describes the Foreign Service's future framework conditions, instruments and tasks, while Chapter 4 reveals the Kingdom of Denmark's strategic interests in relation to both Denmark's multilateral efforts and regional efforts

[2786] Chapter 5 deals with

[2787] Denmark's global commitment in the form of development policy, stabilization efforts and economic diplomacy and contains, among other things, a number of guidelines for a new development policy strategy

[2788] Chapter 6 addresses the question of the future task performance of the Danish Armed Forces based on Denmark's strategic framework conditions, and has been prepared with a view to forming part of the basis for the political discussions on a new defence agreement after

[2789] Against this background, this chapter contains both an overall strategic proposal for core tasks and priorities to promote Denmark's interests and an overall proposal for how to achieve stronger coordination and integrated thinking of Denmark's foreign and security policy, defense policy, trade policy and export promotion, and development policy

[2790] Overall, this report outlines a path forward for safeguarding Denmark's interests and values in the next 10-15 years

[2791] Follow this path

[2792] Danish diplomacy and defense can place Denmark firmly in international cooperation and thus preserve and further develop a safe, free and prosperous Denmark with a Danish foundation of values ​​for the benefit of the population

[2793] Terms of Reference for the study on Danish foreign policy

[2794] Current global developments mean that we are facing a new foreign and security policy reality characterized by political and economic power shifts, a changed threat landscape and greater complexity

[2795] There are new actors with global ambitions and at the same time expectations that the EU will be able to take on a greater role on the international stage

[2796] This development will set the framework for Danish foreign and security policy in the coming 10-15 years - and will both place new demands on us and create new opportunities

[2797] Among the key development trends, challenges and new opportunities of importance to Denmark are: Global power shifts that are gradually shifting economic, political and military power to new actors and centres – not least in Asia

[2798] This development opens up new thinking and new opportunities for influence for Denmark

[2799] New growth in Europe and the US, which will open up opportunities in traditional markets

[2800] The increasing migration towards Europe from weak and unstable states in Africa and the Middle East

[2801] The combination of weak states and instability in the region not only leads to migration but also creates space for terror and organized crime to develop

[2802] The conflicts and increasing violent extremism in the Middle East and North Africa, which have plunged the region into chaos and are creating fertile ground for further extremism

[2803] The conflict between Russia and Ukraine, which is an expression of new geopolitical tensions in Denmark's immediate vicinity

[2804] Russia's actions could lead to renewed instability in Europe and undermine the established European security architecture

[2805] The increasing economic and security significance of developments in the Arctic

[2806] There is a need for continued close cooperation in the Kingdom on the Arctic and on international work

[2807] Developments in the world's poor countries with new actors, new power structures, new vulnerabilities, but also new growth opportunities

[2808] With new UN goals for poverty reduction and sustainable development, development aid must play even better together with other instruments and recipient countries' own needs and contributions

[2809] New threats and global developments, which create a need for continued strong transatlantic cooperation and an increased focus in light of the increasing demand for the Armed Forces' capabilities for international and national task solving, including in the Arctic and in relation to the cyber area

[2810] The government is therefore launching a foreign and security policy investigation

[2811] Based on an assessment of Denmark's strategic interests, the report will present a comprehensive proposal for stronger coordination and integrated thinking of Denmark's foreign and security policy, defense policy, trade policy and export promotion, and development policy

[2812] Furthermore, the report must present an overall strategic proposal for core tasks and priorities to promote Denmark's interests

[2813] The purpose of the study is to create the basis for increased focus and prioritization of Denmark's international engagement and the safeguarding of Denmark's interests, including commercial ones

[2814] The report will, among other things, form the basis for future negotiations on a new defense agreement after 2017 and for a new development policy strategy in 2016. Practice On 15 September 2015, the Government will initiate a foreign policy report in accordance with the Government's Basic Principles

[2815] The investigation is led by Peter Taksøe-Jensen

[2816] The head of the investigation work is placed in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which, together with the Ministry of Defence, provides secretarial assistance dedicated to the purpose

[2817] In addition, the head of the investigation work can draw on the ministries, and they will provide relevant material for the work

[2818] The detailed organization of the assistance is done in consultation with the head of the investigation work

[2819] The government will discuss the status of the investigation along the way

[2820] The investigation must, to the greatest extent possible, build on existing analyses and reports, and current foreign analyses may also be included

[2821] The investigation work will be continuously discussed in a followup group with experts with insight into the area from, among others, organizations and the research community, and the head of the investigation will meet with the established foreign policy forums and the political parties

[2822] The investigation work must be completed by May

[2823] Summary of the Follow-up Group's discussions To support the work on the foreign policy study, a follow-up group was established in accordance with the terms of reference, including experts from the research community and relevant organizations

[2824] During the course of the work on the report, the entire follow-up group met four times and discussed the various aspects of future foreign policy: The theme of the follow-up group's first meeting on 19 October 2015 was the purpose of the report and how to ensure a stronger connection between strategic interests and the implementation of foreign and security policy

[2825] A focal point at the meeting was how to establish a narrative where interests and values can be more clearly expressed in foreign policy as guiding principles for Denmark's efforts

[2826] These discussions were further fleshed out at the follow-up group's second meeting on December 10, where a central theme was the vision for a coherent Danish foreign policy

[2827] The follow-up group also discussed key global development trends, opportunities and challenges in the coming 10-15 years

[2828] The focus was particularly on global power shifts, demographics, and refugee and migration flows

[2829] At the third meeting of the follow-up group on 28 January 2016, the discussions went into depth with Denmark's national interests: It was discussed what Denmark's national interests are and how they can form the basis for focusing and prioritizing Denmark's foreign and security policy efforts

[2830] The follow-up group also discussed how Denmark can become better at integrating the many instruments of foreign policy and thereby achieve the greatest possible impact and long-term effect

[2831] There was a particular focus on stabilization efforts in fragile situations

[2832] At the fourth meeting on March 10, the focus was on future development policy, with presentations on both the UN's 2030 Agenda with the 17 new global goals, as well as the role of business and civil society in development policy

[2833] Finally, the follow-up group gathered the threads from the four meetings and discussed possible mechanisms to ensure stronger strategic thinking

[2834] The discussions on the individual themes were based on oral and written presentations from the members of the follow-up group and the secretariat

[2835] These presentations have led the discussions around all aspects of the investigation work, including security, defense, development and trade policy issues, as well as questions about Denmark's opportunities and challenges in the coming years

[2836] A clear strength of the follow-up group has been the broad composition of members, representing the research community, industry and business organizations, think tanks and civil society

[2837] The discussions in the follow-up group have been open, lively and characterized by great commitment

[2838] There has been ongoing sparring around the central themes of the report

[2839] The work of the follow-up group has thus been of great importance to the investigation, and many of the ideas of the follow-up group have been continued in the investigation. The members' commitment has also been expressed in active participation in the public debate in parallel with the investigation work, just as several follow-up group members have contributed to separate roundtable discussions on more limited aspects of the investigation

[2840] The follow-up group has not been asked to approve the conclusions and recommendations of the investigation, which are solely the responsibility of the investigator

[2850] The follow-up group expressed the hope that the report would come up with a proposal for guidelines or principles for Denmark's foreign policy, and that there should be a popular and political anchoring of such strategic guidelines or principles

[2851] An engaging common narrative about Denmark's external policies can and should be established

[2852] It would therefore be useful to find ways to involve the public in a debate about Denmark's foreign policy

[2853] Precisely by presenting guidelines, principles and recommendations, more forward-looking and principled foreign policy discussions can be set up, even after publication

[2854] Several participants in the follow-up group offered to host debate events

[2855] The report should, as far as possible, be in a widely accessible language

[2856] Several emphasized the inextricable link between national and international politics in that century

[2857] Danish foreign policy cannot therefore be formulated solely on the basis of the national political agenda or solely on the basis of developments outside the country's borders

[2858] Foreign policy should stem both from a narrative - or vision-doctrine - about Denmark's foreign policy identity and be formulated based on the development trends that characterize the world

[2859] There was general support for ensuring a stronger and more pronounced connection between Denmark's core interests and foreign and security policy

[2860] A minimalist approach to national interests, especially avoiding inflation in security interests (threats), was highlighted as a possible path

[2861] Several pointed out the problem of making a sustainable prioritization of interests - it’s easier to prioritize efforts

[2862] Several highlighted values or principles as a continuing central element in Danish interest representation

[2863] Principles were in some areas a more useful concept than values

[2864] With less emphasis on threats (necessity), comes greater importance of visions and choices

[2865] Furthermore, prosperity was pointed out as a core interest – not only as a convenience but also as a prerequisite for being able to translate interests into action in other areas, including safeguarding the nation's security

[2866] In the context of the current resource situation in the foreign, development and defence areas, there was broad support for the report providing a proposal for a sustainable prioritisation tool

[2867] Suggested criteria for whether an area should be prioritized were 1) whether an effort can be linked to Denmark's fundamental interests, 2) whether the area of effort is fragile (whether something is threatened; can fall either way) and 3) whether Denmark can make a difference

[2868] Several also requested a geographical dimension in a prioritization tool

[2869] In parallel with the representation of interests, it was emphasized that Denmark must prioritize its efforts in areas where we have special conditions to make a difference

[2870] It may therefore be useful for the report to both contain analyses of global development trends and to take a position on what type of foreign policy actor Denmark is and what special conditions and opportunities Denmark has for influencing the world

[2871] A methodological distinction was proposed between conditions that Denmark can change itself, conditions that Denmark can change through others, and conditions that Denmark cannot change

[2872] It was also argued that the focus for Denmark was often on positioning rather than impact, which could be better illustrated

[2873] Among the tools identified were alliances/partnerships or concentric circles consisting of countries with common interests in given areas

[2874] It was proposed to strengthen joint efforts between public and private actors, including public and private financing as well as governmental and civil society organizations

[2875] Several also saw the report as an opportunity to point out how important the international order and a strong set of international rules are for Denmark, as a small state, to safeguard its interests, including security interests and economic interests

[2876] There are existing structures and institutions that are often taken for granted, but which are currently undergoing change, partly as a result of the fundamental shift of power from West to East

[2877] The EU, NATO and the UN were mentioned as international organizations that, with their binding nature, can deliver global public goods (e.g. environment, climate, financial stability, conflict resolution, security and trade regimes) on which Denmark depends

[2878] Denmark therefore has a strong interest in engaging in these organizations and actively influencing them

[2879] As far as the EU is concerned, it would also be important in the report to show how the EU can specifically serve as a tool for safeguarding Denmark's interests in the world

[2880] The follow-up group also touched on a number of more specific issues - including the relationship with the USA and China, developments in Denmark's eastern and southern regions, the UN's new global goals and sustainable development, the Arctic and the Danish Commonwealth, and the importance of the foreign service for Danish companies and export promotion

[2881] Summary from the second meeting of the Follow-up Group, December 10, 2015, Eigtveds Pakhus

[2882] There was agreement that a foreign policy vision would be a good starting point for a much-needed determination of Denmark's foreign policy identity

[2883] But you should be sharp and use 'big words' that reflect Denmark's aspirations

[2884] Denmark thrives best in a stable, liberal and regular world order, and best defends Danish interests and values by defending the international system

[2885] Furthermore, the Commonwealth should be promoted as a central part of Denmark's foreign policy 'DNA

[2886] The purpose of foreign policy is twofold: To influence international developments for the benefit of Denmark and to understand developments so that Denmark can best adapt to the reality around us

[2887] Denmark has been largely shaped and has benefited from the outside world, and this should be clearly emphasized

[2888] It would be useful to have a regular process around the vision and priorities in foreign policy, which can contribute to political and popular ownership and a consolidated foreign policy line

[2889] A vision should also highlight that Denmark achieves concrete benefits by cooperating not only with partners, but also through multilateral forums and especially through the EU

[2890] A clear distinction should be made between different forms and levels of partnerships, including between multilateral and supranational organizations, lasting and “less lasting” partnerships, and international structures

[2891] The follow-up group was consistently concerned about the EU's cohesion in the coming years, which several considered a significant challenge

[2892] Regarding global power shifts, the world's economic (and political) center of gravity is moving further towards Asia towards 2030 as a natural consequence of the economic growth in the densely populated Asian countries

[2893] There are several scenarios for the Chinese economy, which on the one hand have enormous potential, but on the other hand also contain uncertainties

[2894] Much will depend, among other things, on continued technological development and a successful transition of the economy to a greater extent also driven by internal demand

[2895] At the same time, Denmark will increasingly have to deal with and cooperate with countries (not only in Asia) that are wholly or partially undemocratic

[2896] The necessary increased emphasis in cooperation with these countries

[2897] will make new demands on Denmark's foreign policy

[2898] One should also not overlook Africa, which does not figure much in global statistics, but which may become increasingly important for Europe, both in terms of opportunities (trade, shipping, etc.) and in terms of risks (conflicts and migration), not least in light of its geographical proximity to Europe. Denmark can and should exploit its advantages through networks, both between states, private actors and large cities

[2899] In several areas, Copenhagen is a more well-known 'brand' than Denmark, and often large cities or states are a more suitable partner for Denmark in terms of size

[2900] Denmark has the potential to be an international 'idea leader' who can help shape solutions to common challenges

[2901] To strengthen Denmark's ability to conduct a coherent foreign policy, a number of concrete initiatives can be considered (among the examples were an Arctic competence center, a stabilization academy or a foreign affairs committee in the government

[2902] Regarding Denmark's experiences with collective thinking and stabilization, however, one should also be careful not to oversell the successes

[2903] It was also noted that Denmark and the Danish business community have far from ceased to be idea-generating

[2904] For example, Danish companies are becoming increasingly better at combining their exports of goods (e.g. wind turbines) with durable services (e.g. online monitoring and maintenance

[2905] Internationalization and participation in global value chains are also becoming more important

[2906] This more complex reality must be reflected in the organization of Denmark's trade policy and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' export promotion efforts

[2907] The discussion on demographic development and migration was based on the fact that people have always migrated, and in a globalized world, this will not decrease in scale

[2908] Today, approximately one billion people are migrants

[2909] The majority migrate locally or regionally, while only a smaller proportion move from south to north

[2910] Behind migration lies both 'push' and

[2911] In Africa, population growth over the coming years will mean that over 50 million people will need to enter the labor market annually

[2912] This places great demands on economic growth and education, but also on politically and environmentally inclusive and sustainable development in societies

[2913] In this context, migration can also be a 'valve' for economic and social unrest, especially in poorer 'sending areas

[2914] At a time when the refugee crisis is very high on the Danish and European agenda, it was important not to forget the positive migration agenda, which is about Denmark and other European countries lacking qualified labor in the coming years

[2915] The domestic debate was currently characterized by a confusion of concepts that confuses refugees, migrants and foreign labor

[2916] It was important to base the debate on a sober data basis

[2917] Summary from the third meeting of the Follow-up Group, January 28, 2016, Eigtveds Pakhus

[2918] The group discussed a model for a more interest-based foreign policy

[2919] Several in the group found such a model necessary in light of the foreign policy framework, while others were more reserved about its applicability in the real world

[2920] It could be useful to focus on the fact that Denmark is actually very well positioned to "contribute to" (and not just "secure itself" in) an increasingly globalized world

[2921] Likewise, there could be a positive definition of national interests rather than emphasizing what they are not

[2922] It was argued that values are a logical prerequisite for determining interests, which in turn were a prerequisite for prioritizing and determining which instruments to use in foreign policy

[2923] This should be clear, and it was argued that Danish values ​​should be defined clearly and consistently

[2924] Several noted in this connection that one could explicitly state that politics is normative, and that determining the fundamental values ​​and interests to be pursued in foreign policy must largely be a political issue

[2925] The report could therefore usefully provide a 'launching platform' for a political and public debate on the priorities

[2926] A few referred to the ongoing work within the EU on the preparation of a new global strategy and the approach to values ​​in that context

[2927] It was argued that an interest model would lead to a technocratic ‘

[2928] which left too little room for engagement and actual discussion

[2929] Others, on the contrary, found that the purpose of the investigation should be a sober and analytical presentation

[2930] There was also a call for an explicit role for development policy and the new global goals in the model

[2931] These were closely linked to the protection of interests and not simply an expression of philanthropy

[2932] Several also emphasized that it was important that an interest model did not appear as a cost-cutting exercise, but as a model that was relevant regardless of the resources available

[2933] It was noted that it could be useful to highlight how resource allocation should be viewed in relation to the possible gains, and that one could thus – in economic terms – see individual initiatives in relation to their marginal costs and marginal benefits

[2934] In this context, it was also argued that capacities and resources could be explicitly included in a prioritization tool. Integrated thinking at the strategic level should not only be seen as cooperation across authorities (whole-of-government), but across both authorities and private actors as a ‘whole-of-society’ approach

[2935] It was noted that coordination between authorities is part of the “Danish model”

[2936] However, several also added that collaboration can be much more effective across authority boundaries, and that silo thinking is still widespread

[2937] Incentive structures that 'force' cooperation could be a possibility

[2938] The Peace and Stabilization Fund (FSF) has provided experience with cooperation on stabilization efforts, particularly between military, humanitarian and developmental efforts

[2939] In popular terms, one could thus direct efforts not only towards poor people, but "poor people who are being shot at

[2940] This could have several benefits: increased security, also for Denmark, better lives for the hardest-hit populations, global benefits in the form of increased order and stability, and closer ties to the allies we cooperate with in the efforts

[2941] This work is difficult in reality, as the experience from Afghanistan shows

[2942] In this context, it was argued that conflicts are ultimately resolved through political negotiations between those involved and not by military means

[2943] Arguments were made for and against using a larger portion of development funds for the FSF. Within development efforts, there was great potential for increased cooperation between authorities and institutional investors, including in relation to risk sharing on the investment side

[2944] Some members called for consideration of whether the various public investment and export support schemes could be coordinated to a greater extent, facilitating access for businesses and investors

[2945] It was also noted that there is a demand in developing countries for investments from countries like Denmark, which typically contribute more to local growth and welfare than, for example, investments from Asian countries

[2946] It was also noted how authorities in the economic field increasingly have to deal with transnational matters, for example within joint taxation agreements

[2947] This could thus also be seen as foreign policy areas or areas where there is a need for increased coherence between foreign policy and domestic conditionsconditions

[2948] Overall, there was a challenge in the increasingly close connections between domestic and foreign policy

[2949] Summary from the fourth meeting of the Follow-up Group, March 10, 2016, Eigtveds Pakhus

[2950] The follow-up group discussed the framework for a new narrative about development policy based on the UN

[2951] s new global goals and the role of business and civil society

[2952] Some believed that the story could be usefully linked more closely to Danish interests and its significance for Denmark in general

[2953] Not because it will in itself make aid efforts more effective, but to make them more visible to the public

[2954] Others believed that Danes feel like part of a global community of destiny

[2955] A new narrative about development policy and foreign policy in general must therefore not only take Denmark or Danish interests as a starting point in order to meet understanding or support among the Danish population. The UN’s Sustainable Development Goals for 2030 were an obvious starting point for Denmark’s future development policy

[2956] The SDGs break with the idea of development cooperation as 'aid' and open a new avenue for public-private partnerships

[2957] Including on financing, where traditional aid can be used as leverage for private investment in developing countries

[2958] It was highlighted that Denmark has something special to offer in policy formulation and regulation, which are central prerequisites for all 17 goals

[2959] Several also saw the global goals and the Paris climate agreement, including the national climate action plans, as obvious opportunities for Danish companies

[2960] There was support for the need to prioritize the 17 goals to ensure impact in the areas where Denmark can make a difference, but also an emphasis on the mutual coherence and complementarity of the goals

[2961] Some highlighted the risk of all countries choosing the same (most attractive) targets, while others found it absolutely necessary for resource-efficient efforts

[2962] In planning development policy, there is a need to distinguish between the level of development and degree of fragility of different countries

[2963] In the most crisis-affected, poorest and most fragile situations, the weight of traditional aid and stabilization efforts will continue to matter a lot

[2964] Conversely, in poor but stable countries and especially in middle-income and emerging countries, there will be fertile ground for public-private partnerships

[2965] Different goals must be pursued in different contexts: poverty alleviation, political progress, security, global commons, prevention of crises that could affect Denmark, etc

[2966] The universal nature of the SDGs provides new opportunities for dialogue

[2967] But they also require that efforts be made in Denmark

[2968] It was argued that Danish/Nordic strengths and societal values are reflected in the goals, and that Denmark can take a leading role

[2969] It was also encouraged to distinguish between actual objectives and more process-oriented goals and sub-goals

[2970] Several parties emphasized a "whole of society" approach to development efforts

[2971] Companies and civil society actors have the funds, knowledge and interest in contributing – and their contribution is necessary to increase the impact of the efforts and make the money go further

[2972] Humanitarian and fragile situations are increasingly the focus of innovative partnerships

[2973] Including refugee camps, where civil society organizations have local knowledge and networks, and Danish companies can contribute with concrete solutions

[2974] There was agreement that investment and trade are an important instrument for promoting sustainable development

[2975] But it must be planned carefully so that development assistance does not become a hidden form of business support, but only contributes to investors' risk hedging

[2976] It was emphasized that investments from a country like Denmark are particularly in demand due to the local roots

[2977] Some found that it would be beneficial to strengthen coordination between or completely merge the existing public financing institutions (IFU, EKF, Vækstfonden) according to foreign models. In relation to the study's treatment of trade policy, it was urged to highlight investments, exports of services, the importance of market access and the need to strengthen free trade in both depth (nearby markets) and breadth (several countries

[2978] Summary of the discussions in the follow-up group • The final discussion in the follow-up group focused on the main conclusions from the follow-up group's four meetings as well as recommendations for the report from the members

[2979] There was general support for a prioritization model and established benchmarks priorities, although some made suggestions for expansion and changes to the priorities

[2980] In general, it was argued that Denmark's physical presence is a prerequisite for prioritized efforts to have an impact

[2981] • Some referred to the fact that the report will be read in relation to the current savings and efficiency discourse, and words such as 'prioritization' and 'focusing' could be perceived as an opportunity for new cuts

[2982] The arguments for an interest-based approach could therefore be clarified

[2983] Several called for an analysis of the development in the resource situation over time, and what consequences this has had for task performance

[2984] It should be made clear that this was a political choice. • In relation to future defence policy, the continued need for a deployable defence was highlighted, as was the need to contribute to military deterrence, although one should not fall into the trap of listening to the ‘senile courage’ of retired Cold Warriors

[2985] Regarding the Arctic, it was argued that territorial defense in the Arctic would be a miscalculation, as any future conflicts could probably take place between major powers in the North Atlantic but unlikely in Greenland

[2986] In relation to the report’s recommendations on strategic integrated thinking, several warned against overselling the concept of 'integrated thinking' as the solution to all challenges, including those related to resources

[2987] It was a slogan everyone could agree on

[2988] A more connected world with more opportunities and challenges gives more tasks to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other institutions – not fewer, and you cannot always rationalize your way out of resource shortages by 'simply' thinking more together

[2989] Several found it important that mechanisms for strategic thinking are broad-based, and that development, business and other considerations are included on an equal footing with classic foreign, defense and security policy considerations

[2990] It was noted that there is an international trend towards establishing mechanisms in the form of national security councils or foreign affairs committees at the government level

[2991] There was broad support for identifying various mechanisms for a continuous, forward-looking and broadly based foreign policy debate

[2992] In this regard, several found that the process of formulating strategies itself was crucial, and it was in this work that new and collaborative thinking emerged

[2993] The impression from the discussions was that, across foreign, security, trade and development policy, etc., a strong and engaging narrative could be established that Danes and politicians can understand, debate and agree on
